messages:
liam: Heads up — saw a weird jump in P99 latency on the small-seqlen paths this morning. Telemetry shows the chooser is routing some short requests to the quant-gemm fallback on A100. Not expected. Anyone else seeing this?

marta: ugh. which telemetry key? can you paste the sample lines?

liam: sure. snippet from /var/log/runtime/chooser.log (redacted):

```
2026-03-18T06:12:04Z INFO chooser:request=abc123 arch=a100 seq_len=16 selected_kernel=quant_gemm reason=mem_estimate_over_threshold(est=1.2MB,bound=1.0MB) flags=[AUTO_TUNE:off, KV_PREFETCH:on] latency_ms=23.4
2026-03-18T06:12:04Z INFO chooser:request=abc124 arch=a100 seq_len=12 selected_kernel=fast_gemm reason=heuristic_score(score=0.82) flags=[AUTO_TUNE:off, KV_PREFETCH:on] latency_ms=8.1
2026-03-18T06:12:05Z INFO chooser:request=abc125 arch=a100 seq_len=8  selected_kernel=quant_gemm reason=mem_estimate_over_threshold(est=0.95MB,bound=0.9MB) flags=[AUTO_TUNE:off, KV_PREFETCH:off] latency_ms=20.2
```

liam: the estimator numbers look jittery around the boundary, so for short seqs it's flipping to quant_gemm which has worse kernel launch overhead here.

craig: hmm sounds like mem estimator config drift. did any autotune flags change? the logs say AUTO_TUNE:off — is that global or per-model?

liam: we set AUTO_TUNE:off at the cluster level for the canary yesterday to test determinism. thought it was isolated to canary nodes. but these traces are from a dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-prod-a100-1).

anjali: quick question — how big is your KV cache hit rate on those requests? if KV_PREFETCH is on but cache cold, mem_estimate spikes can happen.

liam: good call. here's a matching kvstat line for abc123 from the same timeframe:

```
2026-03-18T06:12:04Z INFO kvcache:request=abc123 model=llama-xl cache_hit=false prefetch=thermal miss_penalty_est=3.2KB
```

liam: so cache miss + prefetch set = temporary mem bump. leads estimator to choose quant path.

marta: that explains perf regression. potential mitigations: lower mem_estimate sensitivity, add hysteresis around seq_len boundaries, or enable AUTO_TUNE on those nodes so the chooser learns real latencies.

craig: agree. can we confirm which env var toggles the hysteresis? I remember `CHOOSER_SEQLEN_MARGIN` existed but not sure if it's wired to production.

anjali: `CHOOSER_SEQLEN_MARGIN` is used by the seqlen bucketing code and expects an int (tokens). default is 2. we could bump to 4 for short-seqlen buckets to avoid flip-flop.

liam: i'm going to run a local smoke with `export RUNTIME_DEBUG=chooser:1,kvcache:1` and set `CHOOSER_SEQLEN_MARGIN=4` on a canary node. also re-enable AUTO_TUNE to see if it picks the low-overhead kernel. any objections?

marta: +1 from me. add a metric for "chooser_flips" so we can count how often selected_kernel changes for same model/seqlen within 10s.

craig: can you add a log tag as well so we can filter? like `chooser.flip=true` when decision changed for same request id family.

liam: will do. planning to push patch and run on 2 canary nodes: 
```
-- env: CHOOSER_SEQLEN_MARGIN=4
-- env: RUNTIME_DEBUG=chooser:1,kvcache:1
-- env: AUTO_TUNE=on
```

liam: expected quick check: if flip count drops and p99 latency for seq_len<=16 reduces by ~8-12ms, we roll the margin change.

dev-bot: deploy triggered: canary/chooser-margin-4 -> nodes redwood-dedicated-prod-a100-1a,1b (build 2026-03-18_0615). CI: ✔️.

liam: thanks. i'll post back with initial results in ~30m.

srebot: alert suppressed for p99-spike on a100-pool due to active investigation (owner=liam). remember to re-enable alerts after canary.

liam: quick follow-up (30m): canary shows chooser_flips dropped from 420/h -> 18/h and p99 for seq_len<=16 dropped 11ms median across the two nodes. KV miss rate unchanged (still cold), so margin prevented the noisy estimator from flipping the kernel.

marta: nice! next step: proposal to make margin 3 as global default and add a metric-driven autotune that widens margin during periods of high kv miss rate. file a short RFC?

craig: also want a small change to the logging: include `estimator_confidence` float in chooser log lines so we can later set threshold instead of raw est.

liam: agree on both. i'll open a PR for the margin default and another for including estimator_confidence. will add RFC for the autotune policy.

anjali: thanks all. learning: KV prefetch + cold cache can indirectly bias kernel selection via transient memory estimates — we should add a note to the troubleshooting doc. :memo:

liam: noted. adding doc entry and closing the loop after PR merge. :white_check_mark:
